Create a network graph

Source: R/network_graph.R
network_graph.Rd

Draws a network (a graph) with a force-directed layout: nodes repel each other while the links pull connected nodes together, so that clusters appear on their own. The nodes can be coloured by group and sized by a value (by default by their number of links).

Usage

network_graph(
  data,
  from,
  to,
  weight = NULL,
  nodes = NULL,
  node_id = NULL,
  node_group = NULL,
  node_size = NULL,
  node_label = NULL,
  directed = FALSE,
  colors = NULL,
  node_radius = c(5, 18),
  link_col = "#a7b0ba",
  show_labels = NULL,
  label_font_size = 10,
  charge = -160,
  link_distance = NULL,
  zoom = TRUE,
  legend = TRUE,
  legend_font_size = 11,
  hover = TRUE,
  animate = TRUE,
  title = NULL,
  title_font_size = 16,
  font = "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif",
  bg_col = "white",
  text_col = "#333333",
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of links, one row per link.

from, to

The names of the columns giving the two ends of each link.

weight

Optional. The name of a numeric column giving the strength of each link (drawn as its width).

nodes

Optional. A data frame of nodes, to give them a group, a size or a label (nodes that only appear here are drawn without links).

node_id

The name of the column of nodes that holds the node ids (the values used in from and to). Defaults to its first column.

node_group, node_size, node_label

Optional. Names of columns of nodes giving the group (colour), the size (a number) and the label of each node.

directed

Logical. Draw arrows from from to to. Defaults to FALSE.

colors

Optional. Colours of the groups: one per group or a named vector matched to the groups.

node_radius

The smallest and the largest node radius in pixels. Defaults to c(5, 18).

link_col

The colour of the links. Defaults to "#a7b0ba".

show_labels

Logical. Write the labels next to the nodes. By default every label is shown for networks of up to 40 nodes, otherwise only the labels of the biggest nodes; hovering a node always shows the labels of its neighbours.

label_font_size

The font size of the labels. Defaults to 10.

charge

How strongly the nodes repel each other (a negative number). Defaults to -160.

link_distance

Optional. The preferred length of the links in pixels. By default it grows with the size of the chart and shrinks with the number of nodes.

zoom

Logical. Let the viewer zoom and pan. Defaults to TRUE.

legend

Logical. Show a legend of the groups. Defaults to TRUE.

legend_font_size

The font size of the legend. Defaults to 11.

hover

Logical. Show tooltips and highlight on hover. Defaults to TRUE.

animate

Logical. Let the network settle into place when the chart is drawn (otherwise it is drawn already settled). Defaults to TRUE.

title

Optional. The title of the chart.

title_font_size

The font size of the title. Defaults to 16.

font

The font family. Defaults to "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif".

bg_col

The background colour. Defaults to "white".

text_col

The colour of the text. Defaults to "#333333".

width, height

Optional. The size of the chart.

Value

An r2d3 htmlwidget.

Interactions

Hover a node to highlight its neighbours and see its details; drag a node to move it (the network follows); scroll to zoom and drag the background to pan (zoom). Click a group in the legend to highlight it. The network settles into place when the chart is drawn. Inside Shiny, clicking a node sets input$<id>_clicked to a list with id, label, group and degree.

Examples

# Who works with whom in a small company
team <- data.frame(
  from = c("Ana", "Ana", "Ana", "Ben", "Ben", "Chloe", "Chloe", "Dev",
           "Eve", "Eve", "Farid", "Gus", "Gus", "Hana", "Hana", "Ivo",
           "Jo", "Jo", "Kim", "Ana", "Eve"),
  to = c("Ben", "Chloe", "Dev", "Chloe", "Dev", "Dev", "Eve", "Eve",
         "Farid", "Gus", "Gus", "Hana", "Ivo", "Ivo", "Jo", "Jo",
         "Kim", "Lea", "Lea", "Hana", "Kim")
)
people <- data.frame(
  name = c("Ana", "Ben", "Chloe", "Dev", "Eve", "Farid", "Gus", "Hana",
           "Ivo", "Jo", "Kim", "Lea"),
  team = rep(c("Product", "Engineering", "Sales"), each = 4)
)
network_graph(team, from = "from", to = "to", nodes = people,
              node_group = "team", title = "Who works with whom")



# A directed network: which manufacturers make which classes of cars
mpg <- ggplot2::mpg
pairs <- unique(mpg[, c("manufacturer", "class")])
network_graph(as.data.frame(pairs), from = "manufacturer", to = "class",
              directed = TRUE, charge = -220)
